capex.text: Net cash flow used in investing activities was $3.9 million for the six-month period ended June 30, 2026, compared to net cash flow used in investing activities of $4.8 million for the six-month period ended June 30, 2025. The change in net cash flow used in investing activities was primarily due to proceeds from sale of assets of $1.9 million for the six-month period ended June 30, 2026, and purchases of marketable securities of $1.0 million for the six-month period ended June 30, 2025, which we did not have in the six-month period ended June 30, 2026, partially offset by purchases of property and equipment of $7.0 million for the six-month period ended June 30, 2026 compared to $4.8 million for the six-month period ended June 30, 2025.

Digital Advertising.text: Cost of revenue in our media segment increased to $11.4 million for the six-month period ended June 30, 2026 from $7.9 million for the six-month period ended June 30, 2025, primarily due to the increase in costs associated with the increase in digital advertising revenue and a decrease in gross margins.

intro.text: Entravision is a media and advertising technology company. In the U.S., we provide video, audio and digital marketing services to local and national advertisers through a portfolio of television and radio stations and digital advertising services that target Latino audiences. Our advertising technology business provides programmatic advertising technology and services to advertisers and app developers on a global basis. Entravision is the largest affiliate group of the Univision and UniMás television networks. The term "Entravision" as used in this press release refers to Entravision Communications Corporation. Shares of Entravision Class A Common Stock trade on the NYSE under the ticker: EVC. Learn more about us at entravision.com .

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Of this amount, revenue generated by our media segment accounted for approximately 39%, and revenue generated by our ATS segment accounted for approximately 61% of total revenue.

Of this amount, revenue generated by our media segment accounted for approximately 39%, and revenue generated by our advertising technology & services segment accounted for approximately 61% of total revenue.
Revenue from the largest advertiser represented 9% of the Company's total revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025 .
The Company generated 42 %, 25 % and 27 % and of its revenue from continuing operations outside the United States during the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively (see Note 4).
Our Media segment is a single source for advertisers in our markets.
Our typical customer is a local advertiser that relies on us for planning and executing digital campaigns.
Most of our digital revenue comes from local direct advertisers who rely on us for managed services and consultation to execute complex digital campaigns.
We rely on open-source technologies for certain infrastructure components (e.g., databases) but the core logic is proprietary.
We rely on the accuracy, capacity and security of our IT systems, some of which are managed or hosted by third parties.

We rely on various technologies in our business, including but not limited to our Smadex ad purchasing platform, and the aggregation and analysis of transaction data in our advertising technology & services business.
We rely on sales of advertising time for most of our revenues and, as a result, our operating results are sensitive to the amount of advertising revenue we generate.
Our television and radio operations depend upon maintaining our broadcast licenses, which are issued by the FCC.

Our ability to optimize the delivery of digital advertisements depends on our ability to successfully leverage data, including data that we collect from advertisers, publishers and third parties, as well as our own operating history.

Our future dividend policy, including the amount of any dividend, will depend on factors considered relevant in the discretion of the Board of Directors, which may include, among other things, our earnings, capital requirements and overall financial condition.
